# FBI Employment Eligibility and Criminal Records

Based on my analysis of the FBI Jobs Eligibility Guide 2022, candidates with certain criminal records are automatically disqualified from FBI employment. The specific rules vary depending on the position type.

## Criminal Record Disqualifiers

### For All FBI Positions:
- **Felony Convictions**: Any conviction of a felony is an automatic disqualifier for all FBI positions, regardless of the type of felony. [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)
- The guide explicitly states: "Please note that if you are disqualified by any of the above tests, you are not eligible for employment with the FBI." [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

### For Special Agent Positions:
- The disqualification criteria are stricter for special agent candidates
- In addition to felony convictions, special agent candidates are also automatically disqualified if they have a "conviction of a domestic violence misdemeanor or more serious offense" [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

### For Non-Special Agent Positions:
- While felony convictions are disqualifying for all positions, the document does not explicitly state that misdemeanor convictions (except as they might relate to other disqualifiers like drug policy violations) would automatically disqualify candidates for non-special agent positions [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

## No Exceptions or Time Limitations

Unlike the drug use policies which specify timeframes (such as marijuana use within one year or other illegal drugs within ten years), there are no timeframes mentioned after which criminal convictions would no longer be disqualifying. [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

The document does not mention any exceptions to the felony conviction disqualifier. It explicitly lists this as one of the "specific elements that will automatically disqualify job candidates for employment with the FBI." [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

## Background Investigation Process

All FBI employees must undergo an intensive background investigation to receive an FBI Top Secret security clearance, which includes:
- A polygraph examination
- A test for illegal drug use
- Credit and records checks
- Extensive interviews with former and current colleagues, neighbors, friends, professors, etc. [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

## Other Relevant Disqualifiers

The guide lists several other automatic disqualifiers that could be relevant to individuals with criminal histories, including:
- Violation of the FBI Employment Drug Policy
- Drug use while holding a clearance
- Engagement in prostitution or bestiality
- Failure to pay court-ordered child support
- Failure to file federal, state, or local income tax returns
- Knowingly or willfully engaged in acts or activities designed to overthrow the U.S. government by force [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)

## Conclusion

In conclusion, while candidates with criminal records may technically be able to submit an application, those with felony convictions (or domestic violence misdemeanors for special agent positions) will be automatically disqualified during the screening process according to the FBI's official employment eligibility guidelines. The FBI emphasizes that candidates should ensure they meet all employment requirements and pass all disqualifiers before submitting an application, as these factors are "extensively researched during the FBI background investigation process." [sss.gov](https://www.sss.gov/register/)
